implementation: BootstrapSentinel and Publish are mutually exclusive; both require the existing clean, pushed ecosystem source gate.

Bootstrap binds its inventory and sentinel bytes to the admitted Git commit, rechecks three exact public HTTPS bodies before credential access, then proves the exact FTPS tuple, three remote bodies and reviewed root listing.
Only a previously absent sentinel is staged and promoted under the existing exact operation-owned lease. Existing exact sentinel bytes are verified without overwrite.

Failure recovery removes only a verified prefix at this operation's staging leaf under proven lease ownership. Unexpected bytes, raced final targets and ambiguous lease creation remain for exact review.
NLST reads stop above 65536 bytes, decode strict UTF-8 and ignore only literal self/parent records. Duplicate/case aliases, unsafe names and unregistered colon paths still fail.
Zero-byte FTP bodies retain byte-array type so interrupted empty staging files can be authenticated.
Normal website file, memory, predecessor, catalog, closure and final-marker gates are unchanged. The bootstrap inventory does not admit legacy overlays for website release.

lesson.question: Can the proven account root be bound without requiring a fresh model catalog or accepting unknown website overlays?
lesson.method: Separate tiny identity-marker bootstrap from website release; bind its exact public correspondence and root inventory, then fault-inject actual canonical functions with all state in memory.
lesson.result: Local tests pass, including interruption and identity-substitution failures. No production success claim.
lesson.uncertainty: Actual first write, host recovery behavior and remaining legacy-root reconciliation are unobserved.
lesson.decision: Checkpoint and review bootstrap independently; keep model qualification and actual seed publication as separate required evidence.
lesson.reusable_lesson: Use domain-specific variable names instead of PowerShell automatic variables, and scope Pester mock-count assertions to each test.
